clinical_knowledge.topic: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes trauma-focused psychotherapy; medication options for comorbid symptoms or nightmares require individualized clinician assessment and monitoring.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: nightmares and avoidance of highways 8 months post-crash

Key HPI features: A 47-year-old male presents to the clinic with nightmares and avoidance of highways 8 months post-crash. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Adjustment disorder without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Acute suicidal or homicidal ideation.
management_principles: Offer trauma-focused psychotherapy when clinically appropriate.
A qualified prescriber may consider and monitor medication for target symptoms after reviewing contraindications and adverse effects.
Assess self-harm, violence, and acute safety risk; arrange urgent psychiatric evaluation when risk is imminent.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.
